reason: I want to assemble the focusing mechanism before projecting the stars; the holder should let the lens move.
expectation: I expect a lens in an adjustable holder, though it may need more parts before it can focus the sky.

alternatives.reason: The cloth will provide a screen, but I prefer to prepare the lens first.

effect: The lens assembly is ready; I’ll set up the projection surface next.
reaction: The result was expected, though it did not yet show how focusing works.
reason: The cloth is the only offered combination and should provide a screen for the stars.
expectation: I expect the cloth to be positioned as a projection screen; the lens may still need fitting.

effect: The cloth reveals moving but blurry light, so the lens is the next step toward focus.
reaction: The moving blobs make the need for focusing clear.
reason: The lens assembly is the only offered combination and should sharpen the projection.
expectation: I expect fitting and adjusting the lens to bring the blobs closer to sharp stars.

effect: The lens forms an image of the star disc on the cloth, and sliding it changes where that image is sharp.
reaction: Seeing what the lens does makes the focusing step more meaningful.
reason: The hood is the only offered combination; it may reduce stray light around the lens.
expectation: I expect the hood to make the projected stars easier to see, though the focus may still need adjustment.

effect: The hood reduces stray light, improving contrast between the stars and dark spaces.
reaction: That makes the hood’s purpose clear.
reason: The handle is the only offered combination and should let me turn the star wheel.
expectation: I expect the handle to let me rotate the projected star pattern; it may also complete the goal.

effect: The handle completed the star theatre and revealed that the projected image is upside down.
reaction: The upside-down sky was a satisfying surprise, and linking it to Jo’s old drawing gave the result a sense of purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the focusing lens was most worthwhile: it explained how sliding a lens changes where the disc’s image is sharp.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the lens and holder was useful but rather uneventful on its own.

surprise.text: The finished sky was upside down; that changed my understanding of the projected image.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The hood’s purpose was not certain beforehand, but its effect on contrast was explained.

continue.text: Yes. The clear explanations of focus and contrast made the construction worth the time, and I’d be curious to see how the fair comes together.
